stories.head: British lawmakers warned that the government leans too hard on US cloud companies.
stories.body: Committee chair Chi Onwurah says US law could let Washington switch off British public services. Two US firms may supply most government cloud; ministers say the data stays in Britain.

stories.head: Schneider Electric agreed to buy factory-software maker PTC for 22.6 billion dollars.
stories.body: The French electrical giant pays cash for the Boston firm whose software designs factory products. Regulators must still approve the deal, and Schneider's shares fell about 8 percent in Paris.

stories.head: Qualcomm agreed to pay Chinese rival Huawei for its patents for the first time.
stories.body: The chip makers will share 5G and AI patents, and Qualcomm buys some Huawei patents. Huawei first paid Qualcomm in 2001; the price is secret and US regulators must approve.

stories.head: A Bank of Japan deputy governor says AI may push interest rates to settle higher.
stories.body: Shinichi Uchida called AI a big boost to demand that pushes up prices and growth. If so, central banks may hold rates higher than investors expect; he gave no decision.

stories.head: Hackers posed as an Anthropic employee to slip malware to US AI policy experts.
stories.body: Security firm Proofpoint says a China-linked group invited experts to a made-up advisory committee. Later emails carried malware aimed at cloud accounts; the China link is Proofpoint's own view.

stories.head: Goldman Sachs says local opposition has barely dented its US data center forecast.
stories.body: The bank nudged its estimates up for next year and down for the year after. Data center power use should still grow 38 percent yearly; few Americans want one nearby.

stories.head: TSMC reportedly plans another price rise on its most advanced chips early next year.
stories.body: The biggest contract chip maker reportedly wants up to 6 percent more, after earlier rises. Orders for its newest chip technology reportedly outrun supply; TSMC has not confirmed the report.

stories.head: Germany is paying for tens of thousands of drones that hunt Russian attack drones.
stories.body: Munich firm Quantum Systems will build the drones in Ukraine, Chancellor Merz said in Kyiv. Russia reportedly flies faster jet-powered drones now; exact numbers and delivery dates are not given.

stories.head: Start-up Reflection is said to be readying a strong US-made AI model anyone can run.
stories.body: Unnamed sources say the Nvidia-backed company will publish the model's workings for others to adapt. The model would trail top US systems but rival China's best; nothing is released yet.

stories.head: Korean researchers found AI drug-safety predictors look more accurate than they are.
stories.body: A Gachon University team found near-identical molecules in both training and test data, inflating scores. Accuracy fell when look-alikes were kept apart; the warning comes from one team so far.

stories.head: Sam Altman said the world should accept some harm from AI for its benefits.
stories.body: The OpenAI chief told Politico that he and rival Anthropic differ widely on AI rules. He still rejects catastrophic risks such as losing control of AI; no rule has changed.

stories.head: Stanford researchers set 37,000 AI agents to read old drug trials for success clues.
stories.body: Drugs aimed at genes active in few cell types advanced 40 percent more often. This is a pattern in past records, not proof; the agents ran no lab experiments.

stories.head: McDonald's prices its menu with AI, and some owners say they feel pushed to follow.
stories.body: The models suggest a price for every item at nearly 14,000 US restaurants. Big Mac prices differed by a fifth at nearby stores; McDonald's calls the tool optional.

stories.head: People who teach AI their own jobs say human creativity will keep them employed.
stories.body: Freelancers at Mercor, a firm with over 100,000 AI trainers, think their skills stay safe. Economist Daron Acemoglu warns unemployment could triple in a decade in his worst case.

stories.head: A Florida pizza shop went viral by promising its customers it will never use AI.
stories.body: Munchy's Pizza in Deerfield Beach reached tens of thousands of people with no-AI social posts. Owner Munchy Su has been making pizza since 1991, and the hands stay human.

teaser.head: IBM's quantum chip reportedly did in 19 seconds what a supercomputer needs a century for.
GitHub's former chief launched a code-hosting network spread across many machines.
An analyst says twelve AI-aimed gun turrets now guard Kyiv against Russian drones.
Investors are looking for ways to shield portfolios from the growing weight of AI stocks.

bp.head: Money keeps chasing AI companies even as the cost of borrowing hits a 24-year high.
bp.body: Schneider buys PTC for 22.6 billion dollars; Anthropic reportedly plans a November share sale. Watch US bond rates above 5 percent: the AI rally leans on them.
